name: Availability
question: Can the dataset's own resources be downloaded and opened?
score_0: No resource can be downloaded or opened.
score_1: At least one resource can be downloaded and opened, but at least one other fails (broken link, error page, empty or wrong file).
score_2: Every resource can be downloaded and opens without error.
how_to_check: Download test of every resource except the portal's 'download all' bundle, repeated on a second day before a failure is recorded (fact sheet). A link that leads to a web page instead of the declared file counts as a failure.
typical_fix: Low: correct the link. Medium: restore or upload the file again.
sources: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 (availability)

name: Completeness
question: How many values are missing?
score_0: More than 20% of the cells are empty, or no file can be opened.
score_1: 5-20% of the cells are empty, or at least one column is entirely empty.
score_2: Less than 5% of the cells are empty and no column is entirely empty.
not_applicable: The resources contain no records or attributes, e.g. a raster image or a scanned map; the reason is recorded.
method: automatic for machine-readable files; manual otherwise
how_to_check: Share of empty cells in the most recent machine-readable file (fact sheet). Placeholders such as '-', 'N/A' or '..' count as empty. For data published only as documents (e.g. tables in PDF), estimated by inspection.
typical_fix: Medium: complete the file or state why values are missing.
sources: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 (completeness)

name: Consistency
question: Are the values recorded in the same way throughout the dataset?
score_0: Inconsistencies that prevent analysis without manual work (e.g. values shifted between columns, different units mixed in one column), or no file can be opened.
score_1: Minor inconsistencies: mixed date or number formats in a column, numbers stored as text, different column names or order between files of the same dataset.
score_2: Each column has one type, format and unit, and all files of the dataset share the same structure.
not_applicable: The resources contain no records or attributes, e.g. a raster image or a scanned map; the reason is recorded.
how_to_check: Column types and formats (fact sheet); comparison of the headers of the files of the dataset; inspection of a sample of rows.
typical_fix: Medium: harmonise the files.
sources: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 (consistency); W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP13

name: Plausibility of values
question: Are the values plausible?
score_0: Systematic errors: coordinates outside Greece or in an undeclared reference system, dates in the future, values in the wrong columns; or no file can be opened.
score_1: Isolated implausible values (fewer than 1% of the records), e.g. negative counts or outliers that look like typing errors.
score_2: No implausible values in the automatic checks and in a manual review of 10 random records.
not_applicable: The resources contain no records or attributes, e.g. a raster image or a scanned map; the reason is recorded.
how_to_check: Range checks (fact sheet): coordinates, dates, negative values, duplicates; review of 10 random records; comparison with the publisher's website where the same figures appear. Accuracy against reality cannot be verified in general, so the criterion records plausibility.
typical_fix: Medium: correct the values. High: correct the source system.
sources: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 (accuracy)

name: Timeliness
question: Is the dataset updated as often as its metadata declare?
score_0: The newest data are older than three update periods, or no frequency is declared and there has been no update for more than 12 months.
score_1: The newest data are one to three periods late, or no frequency is declared but the dataset was updated in the last 12 months.
score_2: Updated within the declared frequency (with one period of tolerance), or declared as not updated (one-off or historical data) with a description that says so.
how_to_check: Declared update frequency (metadata) against the date of the newest data: the latest date inside the data where there is one, otherwise the modification date of the newest resource.
typical_fix: Low: declare the actual frequency. High: set up regular updates.
sources: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 (currentness); W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP21; DCAT-AP 3.0.1 (frequency)

name: Format (5-star scale)
question: What is the most open format in which the data are offered?
score_0: Only unstructured formats (PDF, word-processor documents, images, web pages) or map views without data (WMS): 1 star.
score_1: Structured but vendor-specific formats (XLS, XLSX, SHP, MDB) or vendor-specific services (Esri REST): 2 stars.
score_2: At least one open, non-proprietary structured format (CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, XML, GML, KML, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF, NetCDF, RDF) or a download service in such a format (WFS, API): 3 stars or more.
how_to_check: Formats of the resources (fact sheet), checked against the actual content of the files: a file declared as CSV that is in fact a PDF counts as PDF.
typical_fix: Medium: publish an open format next to the existing one.
sources: 5-star Open Data (Berners-Lee); W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP12 and BP14; Directive (EU) 2019/1024, Art. 5

name: Mandatory metadata
question: Are the metadata that DCAT-AP makes mandatory present and meaningful?
score_0: A mandatory element is missing: title, description, or an access URL for a resource.
score_1: All are present, but the description repeats the title or is shorter than 100 characters.
score_2: Title, a meaningful description (at least 100 characters, saying what the data contain) and an access URL for every resource.
how_to_check: Portal metadata (fact sheet): title, length of the description, access URL of each resource. Whether the description is meaningful is confirmed by reading it.
typical_fix: Low: complete the metadata.
sources: DCAT-AP 3.0.1 (mandatory properties of Dataset and Distribution); Ministerial Decision 11654/2026

name: Recommended metadata
question: How many of seven descriptive metadata are present: keyword, theme, publisher, contact point, geographical coverage, temporal coverage, update frequency?
score_0: Two or fewer.
score_1: Three to five.
score_2: Six or seven.
how_to_check: Portal metadata (fact sheet). The first six are recommended properties of DCAT-AP; the update frequency is optional in DCAT-AP and is checked because the assessment of timeliness (Q5) depends on it.
typical_fix: Low: complete the metadata.
sources: DCAT-AP 3.0.1; W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP1 and BP2; Circular 24849/2026

name: Controlled vocabularies
question: Are theme, file format and update frequency given with terms of the controlled vocabularies?
score_0: None of them.
score_1: Some of them; the rest are free text.
score_2: All of those present use controlled vocabularies.
how_to_check: DCAT export of the dataset (data.gov.gr/dataset/<name>.jsonld): theme from the EU data-theme vocabulary, format from the EU file-type vocabulary or the IANA media types, frequency from the EU frequency vocabulary.
typical_fix: Low: select the terms from the vocabularies.
sources: DCAT-AP 3.0.1 (controlled vocabularies); W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP15

name: Licence
question: Is an open licence declared clearly for all resources?
score_0: No licence, or a licence that restricts re-use (non-commercial, no derivatives, permission required).
score_1: An open licence, but not declared for every resource, given only as text without a link, conflicting between resources, or more restrictive than CC BY 4.0 (e.g. share-alike).
score_2: Every resource carries, directly or through the dataset, the link of CC0, CC BY 4.0 or an equivalent or less restrictive open licence.
how_to_check: Licence of the dataset and of each resource in the portal metadata; in case of conflict, the terms on the publisher's website.
typical_fix: Low: declare the licence in the metadata.
sources: Directive (EU) 2019/1024, Art. 8; Regulation (EU) 2023/138, Art. 4; Ministerial Decision 11654/2026, Art. 8; W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP4

name: Free access
question: Can the data be obtained free of charge and without registration?
score_0: A charge applies, or access requires an account that is not open to everyone.
score_1: Free of charge, but registration, an API key or acceptance of additional terms is required.
score_2: Free of charge and without registration.
how_to_check: During the download test and on the publisher's pages linked from the dataset.
typical_fix: High: change of the access policy.
sources: Directive (EU) 2019/1024, Art. 6 and Art. 14; Ministerial Decision 11654/2026, Art. 8

name: Mode of distribution
question: How are the data made available, in the order of preference of the Ministerial Decision: API, direct link, structured file, unstructured file?
score_0: Only through a web page or an application without download, or no working access.
score_1: Files that do not give the complete data through a direct link: split into many parts, or reachable only through an intermediate page, form or map viewer.
score_2: An API, or a stable direct link to the complete data.
how_to_check: Type and address of each resource (fact sheet): API or download service; direct download link; landing page or viewer.
typical_fix: Medium: publish a direct link to the complete data. High: build an API.
sources: Ministerial Decision 11654/2026, Art. 5; W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP17 and BP23

name: Persistent identifier
question: Do the dataset and its resources have stable identifiers?
score_0: No stable address: the dataset or its resources are reachable only through temporary or session-based links.
score_1: The dataset has a stable address, but its resources point to links that change (new address with every upload, query or session parameters).
score_2: The dataset has a stable URI and identifier, and its resources have stable links.
how_to_check: URI and identifier of the dataset in the DCAT export; addresses of the resources (fact sheet).
typical_fix: Low: assign stable addresses.
sources: W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP9 and BP10; DCAT-AP 3.0.1 (identifier)

name: Personal data
question: Does the dataset avoid exposing personal data?
score_0: Personal data of natural persons (names, identity or tax numbers, home addresses, personal contact details) are published without a stated legal basis.
score_1: Indirect identification is possible (e.g. very small counts, exact locations linked to individuals) and the dataset does not state how it was anonymised.
score_2: No personal data; or personal data published under a legal obligation that the metadata state; or data aggregated or anonymised, as stated.
how_to_check: Inspection of the columns and of 10 random records; description and documentation of the dataset.
typical_fix: Medium: remove or aggregate the fields.
sources: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR); Directive (EU) 2019/1024, Art. 1(4); Ministerial Decision 11654/2026, Art. 7

name: High-value designation
question: Do the metadata mark the dataset as high-value?
score_0: No marking: the dataset is high-value by content only.
score_1: Partial marking: the category without a reference to Regulation 2023/138, the reference without the category, or only the high-value dataset type.
score_2: High-value category and a reference to Regulation 2023/138 as applicable legislation.
how_to_check: Fields hvd_category, applicable_legislation and dcat_type of the portal metadata.
typical_fix: Low: complete the metadata.
sources: Regulation (EU) 2023/138, Art. 3; DCAT-AP HVD

name: API and bulk download
question: Is the dataset available both through an API and as a bulk download, as the Regulation requires?
score_0: Neither an API nor a bulk download of the complete dataset.
score_1: Only one of the two, or an API without public documentation and terms of use.
score_2: An API with public documentation and terms of use, and a bulk download of the complete dataset.
how_to_check: Data services of the portal linked to the dataset (access_services), services of the publisher, and download links of the complete data.
typical_fix: Medium: publish a complete download. High: build an API.
sources: Regulation (EU) 2023/138, Art. 3 and Annex; W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP17, BP23 and BP25

name: Machine-readable structure
question: Can a program read the data directly, without manual cleaning?
score_0: Not without manual work: PDF or scanned documents, images, spreadsheets laid out for printing (merged cells, several tables in one sheet), or no data file.
score_1: Readable after minor cleaning: title or note rows above the table, a totals row, numbers stored as text, a header split over two rows.
score_2: One header row, one record per row and one value per cell, without notes or totals inside the table; or a standard structured format (GeoJSON, JSON, XML) that is read without errors.
how_to_check: Automatic read test of the most recent machine-readable file (fact sheet), then a look at the file.
typical_fix: Medium: restructure the file.
sources: W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP12; GDS (2026), Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI; Wickham (2014), Tidy Data

name: Documentation of the structure
question: Is the meaning, type and unit of every field documented (data dictionary)?
score_0: No documentation: the meaning of the fields or codes has to be guessed.
score_1: Partial: the field names are clear but units or codes are not explained, or only some fields are documented.
score_2: Every field has a description, type and unit, and the codes are explained, in the metadata, in a data dictionary or on a page linked from the metadata.
how_to_check: Description, documentation resources and publisher pages linked from the dataset, compared with the columns of the file.
typical_fix: Low: write a data dictionary.
sources: W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP3; GDS (2026), Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI; Gebru et al. (2021), Datasheets for Datasets; MLCommons Croissant 1.0 (RecordSet, Field)

name: Historical depth
question: Are earlier periods or versions of the data available?
score_0: Only the current state; earlier data have been replaced or removed.
score_1: Some earlier periods or versions, with gaps or in a different structure.
score_2: A continuous series of earlier periods or versions in the same structure.
not_applicable: The dataset describes a single fixed moment by design (e.g. a historical map) and is not updated.
how_to_check: Resources per period, temporal coverage in the metadata, archive pages of the publisher.
typical_fix: Medium: publish the archive.
sources: W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP7 and BP8; GDS (2026), Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI

name: Description in Croissant or a datasheet
question: Can the dataset be described in Croissant, or with a datasheet, from the information available?
score_0: Neither: a licence or a machine-readable distribution is missing, and the documentation does not say what the data contain or how they were collected.
score_1: A valid Croissant description at dataset level only, without the fields, or a datasheet with major gaps.
score_2: A valid Croissant description that includes the fields with their types and meaning, or, for data without records, a datasheet that states what the data contain, how they were collected and for which uses they are suitable.
how_to_check: Croissant file generated from the portal metadata and the file structure and validated with the mlcroissant library; the fields are described with the information found under AI2.
typical_fix: Low: complete the metadata and the data dictionary.
sources: MLCommons Croissant 1.0; Gebru et al. (2021), Datasheets for Datasets

name: Suitability for retrieval (RAG)
question: Can the content be split into self-contained pieces that an AI system can retrieve and cite?
score_0: Not usable: scanned images or maps without text, or no content that can be extracted.
score_1: Usable after conversion (text extraction from a born-digital PDF, flattening of a spreadsheet), or the pieces lack a stable identifier or a link to the source.
score_2: Records or text passages with a stable identifier and a link to the source, in text that is extracted cleanly in UTF-8, Greek included.
how_to_check: Text extraction test and check of the Greek encoding (fact sheet); presence of an identifier per record.
typical_fix: Medium: publish the content as structured text or records.
sources: GDS (2026), Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI (unstructured data); W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP10

name: Linkage through common identifiers
question: Can the data be joined with other datasets through common codes or coordinates?
score_0: No identifiers or location information that allow linkage.
score_1: Only names (e.g. municipality names) or codes internal to the publisher, or coordinates without a declared reference system.
score_2: Standard codes (e.g. municipality codes of the Kallikratis classification, NUTS or LAU codes, KAD/NACE activity codes, tax or GEMI numbers, KAEK cadastral codes) or coordinates in a declared reference system.
how_to_check: Column names and values (fact sheet); reference system of the geospatial files.
typical_fix: Medium: add the standard codes.
sources: W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP10 and BP15; FAIR I3

name: Declared limitations
question: Do the metadata or the documentation state the known limitations of the data?
score_0: No statement about coverage, gaps, collection method or known errors.
score_1: A partial statement, e.g. only the source or only the coverage.
score_2: Coverage, gaps, collection method and known errors or changes of method are stated.
how_to_check: Description, documentation resources and linked publisher pages.
typical_fix: Low: add a short note on limitations.
sources: Gebru et al. (2021), Datasheets for Datasets; GDS (2026), Guidelines and best practices for making government datasets ready for AI; W3C Data on the Web Best Practices (2017), BP6
